pageCache.pageTitle: RAF Benson Community Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Welcome back to a new school year! We have a lot of exciting things happening so keep an eye on our class webpages.
Welcome
A warm welcome awaits you at RAF Benson Community Primary School.
I am extremely proud to lead a team that is committed to providing the very best opportunities for the children who attend RAF Benson Primary. Staff, supported by governors and the local community, work hard to deliver a rich and challenging curriculum; to prepare children for future education; and to help them acquire the skills and enthusiasm needed to pursue learning for the rest of their lives.
We are a Local Authority school situated in the heart of the base at RAF Benson. Although almost 100% of our roll are Service children; our school is open to all children in the local area regardless of whether they have a family member in the military. Arrangements can be made for non-service families to gain access to the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: RAF Benson Community Primary School - Childcare Provision
pageCache.text:
Childcare Provision
This page lists the childcare provision within our school community for parents needing wrap around care before and after school.
If you are new to the area and would like to be added to the list on this page, please complete the form in the link below (please note that you must be Ofsted registered): http://goo.gl/forms/cK6h66Irjb
RAF Benson Station Nursery
The Station Nursery at Benson is based on the domestic site, caring for over 100 children at any time in a purpose built secure setting with extensive outdoor play space. The building and equipment has recently been upgraded owing to a change in management and the setting now offers state of the art play and learning materials as well as a purpose-built outdoor area.
The nursery is open to all families from RAF Benson, as well as the local civilian community. They offer full or part time care, as well as shorter pre-school sessions for 3-4 year olds. A breakfast club, after school club, and holiday club are also available for 4-11 year olds, with drop-off and collection available for RAF Benson Community Primary School. Fresh home-cooked meals are provided.
A discount is offered for families of personnel based at RAF Benson and a sibling discount is available where more than one child from the family attends the nursery on a regular basis.
Address: 4Children, Station Nursery, RAF Benson, Near Wallingford, Oxon OX10 6AA Manager: Michelle Telephone: 01491 825082

pageCache.pageTitle: RAF Benson Community Primary School - Separated Parents
pageCache.text:
Separated Parents
Families break up for a variety of reasons; with those breakups can often come heartache and pain for the adults involved.
However, it is not only the adults that suffer, children can go through a grieving process as well. They recognise and feel the loss of the physical presence of one parent and the emotional security that comes with both parents' involvement in day to day life. As well as this, children can feel the loss of the future they imagined that they would have.
It is possible, though, for parents to work with each other to support their child through this process - even when feelings are strong and the future looks difficult. Our Pastoral Support Officer, Mrs Pring can support families in ensuring that children have the best possible outcomes in these situations.
We understand that family breakdowns are difficult and may sometimes require some form of legal intervention such as orders and arrangements from the court. In these circumstances, we will require copies of any court order or arrangements so that we are able to support children and families as best as we can.
Co-Parenting Sessions
We would be happy to support a referral to SSAFA for Service Families in agreeing practical and emotion free routines, boundaries and communication routes that will enable children to have fulfilling and constructive relationships with both parents. They will work with parents in a confidential way to plan and review arrangements until a system is running smoothly.
Rights and Responsibilities
Mrs Pring can advise, find the right advice or signpost parents to advice about their parental responsibilities and rights. Children deserve a relationship with each parent if it is at all possible.
Communication with / from the School
The School App is used to distribute information and news from school and activities that are taking place. We do expect all parents to download the app and this extends to any non-resident parents enabling them to keep up to date with what is happening in school.
Reports
Non-resident parents are entitled to a copy of children's school reports. In order to receive this, they must register their address with the school office who will make sure a copy is posted or emailed out.
Non-resident parents are also entitled to contact the school office via phone or email for information and advice and, if necessary, can make an appointment to see the class teacher after school.
Parents' Evenings
So that both parents can be equally informed about children's progress, we do expect separated parents to attend Parents' Evenings together. This means that both parents hear the same thing and there is no room for different interpretations. Where parents might find joint attendance to be emotionally difficult, Mrs Pring or Mrs Fawdry will attend appointments with both parents to help both get what they need from the session. Please request this in advance as appointment times may be limited.
We do not offer different sessions for separated parents unless there is a court order banning one party from contact with the child and/or the other parent. Our concern is, and always will be, the child's well being and development.

pageCache.pageTitle: RAF Benson Community Primary School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
The 'RAF Benson' school curriculum has to be unique so that we continue to engage and motivate our children as confident, resilient and successful life-long learners wherever in the country or the world they will move next.
We have a strong child-led curriculum so that we avoid disengaging children in learning when they come to us by visiting a topic they have already done in a previous school. Our school attendance is excellent and we believe that having an exciting and interesting curriculum contributes to this!
This page is designed to give you further information about the different elements of our school curriculum. Just click on one of the pages below to know more.

pageCache.pageTitle: RAF Benson Community Primary School - Forest School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
Each week, whatever the weather, a group of very excited children head off to the nearby woods. On arrival, they spend the afternoon creating, collaborating and having fun! Forest School is an activity that we believe supports positive well being in our children and promotes self esteem and confidence. The experience allows children to have 'hands-on' opportunities that they may not be able to have at school or home.
The sessions are not activity based but instead are led by the interests of the learners. Children may enjoy such experiences as building shelters, woodland craftwork, telling stories, cooking over fires, climbing trees, hunting for minibeasts and making mud pies. As the programme develops woodland tools are introduced to extend learning and provide new opportunities for risk management.
The concept was developed in Scandinavia, and operates on the principle that children of all ages benefit from the learning opportunities present in a woodland environment. They found that by taking the majority of their learning outdoors, whatever the weather, their children became resilient, confident and independent learners.

pageCache.pageTitle: RAF Benson Community Primary School - Oxfordshire Supporting Service Children
pageCache.text:
Oxfordshire Supporting Service Children
Currently, our Headteacher, Mrs Fawdry, sits on the National Executive Advisory Committee for Service Children in State Schools and therefore in a position to help and advise local schools on how they can best support Service Children in their schools too.
We aim to meet each term (3 times a year) online or in person and discuss issues relating to mobility and deployment, pastoral support and other issues connected with supporting Service Children.
Locally, there have been a number of events where Service children have got together to celebrate their uniqueness. Camo day and our Service Pupil Act of Remembrance at the beautiful Dorchester Abbey to name just two. We have also worked with other organisations to create a conference for adults to know how to best support Service children and also for children to get together to share their experiences with others.
Should you wish to know more, please contact Mrs Fawdry on 01491 836460.
